title: A modelled answer answers its question
statement: A modelled answer must answer the question asked, picking one of the choices an either-or question offers, never defining the question's words or answering a neighbouring question.
detail: Reported live on a Grade 3 reading build: a modelled row asked whether characters were brave or reckless and its answer card gave two dictionary definitions, and another row asked about one character and answered about another. The build's schema calls both the same failure, the card written from the row's topic rather than from its question, so the child watches a model that never lands. Its rule now requires each modelled answer to answer its own question, name a character the question names, pick one of the choices an either-or question offers and not dodge into defining a word the question already used, and a gate pins it.
